chunks: Ali narrated from his father, from al-Nu'fali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The wound (or blood money for a wound) is not inherited.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report should be understood to mean that it is not inherited in the same way property is inherited, such that each of them takes their share, even though each of the heirs has the right to claim the full amount in its entirety.

key_terms.الحَدُّ: Wound or the compensation (diyah) paid for it

ai.seo_question: Is blood money for a wound inherited by heirs like other property?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that *al-hadd* (compensation for wounds) is not treated as a divisible estate (*māl*) distributed by fixed shares, but rather as a personal right that each heir can individually pursue to its full extent. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Furaykati provides the juristic rationale, distinguishing between the collective inheritance of wealth and the individual capacity of heirs to claim the complete compensation, reflecting the Shia principle that certain financial rights remain attached to the specific victim or their direct representatives rather than being pooled. This distinction is crucial in *fiqh al-mirāth* for determining whether a debt or compensation is settled collectively or pursued individually by heirs.
